chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon the people when they will complain to their Lord.' I said, 'And how do they complain to their Lord?' He said: 'The man will say,
ai.seo_question: How do people complain to God about their wealth according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies a spiritual malaise where individuals attribute their sustenance entirely to their own capital, forgetting that the very source of their wealth is divine. This critique of materialistic self-sufficiency underscores the Shia emphasis on recognizing God as the ultimate provider (Ar-Razzaq), reminding believers that all profit and consumption are ultimately gifts from the Creator rather than mere fruits of human effort.
